title: The Bullet Holes That Fooled The Generals

lines.text: bombers that came home, riddled with bullet holes!
The generals look at the damage and say, armor the holes!
But a mathematician named Abraham Wald stops them.
He asks one strange question: where are the planes that never came back?
Every hole on this plane is a hit it survived.
The planes hit in the engines crashed, so they are missing from the data.
Those clean spots are not safe, they are deadly.
So Wald tells them to armor the engines, where there are no holes at all.
The military listens to his math, and the planes get tougher.
That mistake has a name: survivorship bias.
We only study the winners, and ignore everyone who vanished.
So next time you hear a success story, ask who is missing.
